paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. In this passage, the people don't make the glory of the LORD show up. Moses tells them what to bring and says, "For today the LORD will appear to you." (Leviticus 9:4) They do exactly what the LORD commanded, and then the glory of the LORD appears to all the people. (Leviticus 9:23)

Now look at who goes first. Aaron makes a sin offering for himself before he does anything for the people. (Leviticus 9:7-8) Even the priest needed atonement, and I think that should make every one of us breathe easier. If the man standing at the altar needed a way to come near, then I'm not going to pretend I don't, friend. I could stand at that altar all day with my mustache hanging out and still need it.

Then the fire comes out from the presence of the LORD, and the people shout for joy and fall facedown. (Leviticus 9:24) That's what it looks like when God draws near to people He has made a way for. So here's what to take with you, baker: come to the LORD the way He says, and expect Him to meet you. This story isn't over, either. The priests have only just begun their service.
